evidence.excerpt: IEEE 1149.4 extends boundary-scan to analogue pins, but its adoption in volume production has been limited by uncertainty about achievable fault coverage on practical board topologies. This study analyses test coverage attainable under the 1149.4 standard for five analogue subcircuit categories: RC filters, op-amp stages, ADC input conditioning networks, power management feedback loops, and sensor signal conditioning chains. Each category was represented by ten reference circuits implemented on test vehicles. Coverage was measured by fault injection: 1,240 resistor opens/shorts and 880 capacitor deviations spanning ±20 % to ±80 % of nominal value. Achieved coverage ranged from 73 % for power-management loops to 94 % for RC filter networks, with the main limitation being the bandwidth of the analogue test bus relative to circuit operating frequency. A set of design-for-test recommendations is derived from the results, targeting layouts that improve 1149.4 coverage by an average of 11 percentage points.
